mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags on the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of >1% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and S&P 500 returns in the prior 12 months suggests a wealth effect channel; when PAYEMS growth accelerates above 0.5% monthly for two consecutive months, it predicts continued positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of two consecutive months with PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a synchronized collapse in demand for goods and new construction, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days: higher-than-expected unemployment (vs. prior month) predicts negative returns, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises versus the prior month, across all regimes.
